VILLENA Punong Barangay Barangay San Vicente San Pedro, Laguna Dear PB Villena: DILG Legal Opinion No. 94 s. 2011 DEC 05 2011 This has reference to your 28 October 2011 letter requesting this Department's opinion on the following: a. Whether or not said barangay may continue implementing Barangay Ordinance No. 02-97 notwithstanding DILG MC No. 2011-122 which prohibits the imposition of pass through fees; and b. If in the negative, to advise said barangay on how to regulate the passage of heavy trucks in subdivisions within their area of jurisdiction. Based on your letter and its attachments, the developers and homeowner associations of Pacita Complex I, Pacita II-Phase 1 and 2, Chrysanthemum Village and Rosario Complex, San Vicente, San Pedro, Laguna turned-over the road networks of these subdivisions to the municipal government of San Pedro, Laguna. To protect these road networks, the Sangguniang Barangay of San Vicente, San Pedro, Laguna enacted an ordinance on 15 March 1997 allowing only light and medium vehicles to use said roads. It provided a penalty of not less than PhP500.OO but not more than PhPIOOO.OO, to be determined by the Court, for every violation of said ordinance. The ordinance also provided for an "out-of-court" settlement of any offense involving a violation of the ordinance at a penalty less than that imposed by the ordinance. You now seek the Department's opinion on the implementation of aforesaid ordinance vis-å-vis DILG MCs suspending the collection of illegal fees and taxes, namely: MC Nos.Q007-70, 2009-70, 2009-76, and 2011-122. It must be emphasized that an ordinance enacted by the local sanggunian generally enjoys the presumption of validity, as in this case. Nevertheless, for purposes of aiding barangay San Vicente, San Pedro, Laguna, we shall only provide you with our observation on your ordinance vis-å-vis the imposition of a pass through fee, to wit: • A pass through fee is a tax, fee or charge imposed upon goods carried into, out of, or passing through the territorial jurisdiction of the local government unit; the subject ordinance imposes a penalty for violation of an ordinance allowing only light and medium vehicles to use the road networks :

the regulation of the use of a local road network for purposes of protecting the property right of the barangay, as in this case. For this purpose, a reasonable penalty may be imposed by the barangay for violators of the ordinance. However, the amount of the fine should not be left to the discretion of the designated collector to prevent abuses. We hope the foregoing sufficiently addresses your concern. Very truly yours, sus Director o 1
